<!-- Established facts, one line each, with the source. Grouped by area. Read at session start; cite by area and line rather than restating in chat. -->

# Facts on record

## Execution model

- Two execution paths share parser and phases and differ at the end: the walk interpreter (`fortress file.fss`) and the bytecode compiler (`fortress compile` + `run`) (`repo-internals.md:95-129`).
- The static type checker (Scala, `scala_src/typechecker/`) runs only on the compile path; `walk` turns it off and there is no switch to make it run in the interpreter (`repo-internals.md:127`); every "type error" seen from the interpreter is a run-time dispatch failure.
- `fortress typecheck` checks against `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi`, not the interpreter's prelude, so it is not an oracle for interpreter programs (ledger row 69); making the checker usable on interpreter programs means giving it the interpreter's prelude, which is not a ledger row and not on the worklist as a separate item (it falls under worklist item 2, compiler-path library parity).
- The compiled path measured 6.8× on a scalar `RR64` loop, 8.9× on object-allocating code, 8× on startup, numerics identical (`compiled-path-gaps.md:45, 100-101`); what blocks it is its 592-line prelude (no `List`, no generic `array`, no `exp`/`log`, no `SUM`, an empty `Matrix`), not code generation (rows 71-82).
- The code generator lowers every type to a JVM reference type: `RR64` to the runtime class `FRR64`, no `dadd`/`dmul` anywhere in the generated loop (shown in bytecode, `perf-probes/boxing/javap/`); arrays are library objects over `get`/`put`, not `double[]` (`repo-internals.md:129`).
- **On microGPT-shaped code, boxing is the dominant representational cost, and nothing microGPT-shaped runs on the compiled path today** (measured 2026-09-15, `perf-probes/kernels/REPORT.md`, which corrects the boxing probe's scalar-loop conclusion below as Pavol suspected): the three kernels the program is made of (a 4192-element dot product, a 16×16 matrix product, the row lift with `rmsn`) all fail to compile with `Array is undefined`, `Vector is undefined`, `Array3 is undefined` in `FlatArrays.fsi` (77 errors): the compiler prelude lacks the array TYPES, not only the constructor (wider than ledger row 72; ledger row 305). In Java models of those kernels, boxing as the runtime boxes costs 6.3× (dot), 6.5× (matrix), 2.6× (row lift) over `double[]`, because array element results escape and cannot be scalar-replaced; the generic array object adds only 1.6-9% on top. On the interpreter, the only path that runs them, 43.5% is the AST walk, 32.3% environment lookup, 5.2% type dispatch, 0% number representation (JFR on `krows`). A fairly written scalar loop (literals hoisted, no `:=`) compiles to 9.7× primitive Java; JFR on the real compiled run puts 88.9% of the mutable-variable loop under `BaseTask.inATransaction()`'s eagerly built debug string (`BaseTask.java:248`, `Thread.toString()` through `StringBuilder`). Order that follows: (1) an `RR64` array type in the compiler library (G2) so the kernels exist on that path; (2) the two one-line defects, the debug string and `FFloatLiteral`'s String round-trip; (3) unboxing and `double[]`, where the remaining ~6× on array code lives, designed into (1) rather than retrofitted. Also: a local function does not compile (`Can't compile LetFn`, `CodeGen.java:1552`, ledger row 304); a failed compile leaves a 0-byte jar in the bytecode cache.
- Rung 0's two fixes took the eager debug string (row 302) and `FFloatLiteral`'s String round trip (row 303) out of the scalar loop, so the boxing probe's own reading of the unrepaired tree — 156× primitive Java, of which boxing was about 2 %, with `countedseqloop`'s boxed indices and closure call (about 7 %) and the representational rest (about 30 %) still unaddressed — is history (`FACTS-history.md` § Execution model; `perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md`).
- **The two one-line runtime defects are fixed** (2026-09-17, rung 0 of the plan, `compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`, `before.out`/`after.out`): guarding `BaseTask.inATransaction()`'s debug message with the `debug` flag it already had (`BaseTask.java:248`, ledger row 302) takes the compiled `bench1h`, the loop whose literals are hoisted so the transaction check is the only defect left in it, from **8.8159 s to 0.7287 s** (loop-only medians of 3, JDK 25, 20 M iterations, same freshly rebuilt library jars on both sides).
- **Caching the `double` in `FFloatLiteral`** instead of keeping the literal as a `String` and re-parsing it in `asRR64()` (ledger row 303) takes the compiled `bench1t`, which builds both float literals inside the loop, from **13.0566 s to 0.7384 s**; the literals' own share, the `bench1t` minus `bench1h` difference, falls from 4.2407 s to 0.0097 s, so the per-iteration decimal round trip is gone (2026-09-17, `compile-ladder/rung0/`). The gate after both edits: `ant testFast` 1,377 tests, `ant testSystem` 382 tests, zero failures and zero errors.
- The benchmark numbers on record from 2026-09-15 (`bench1t` 9.3441 s, `bench1h` 6.0732 s) were taken on a quieter machine; the 2026-09-17 before-run of the same unmodified tree measured 13.0566 s and 8.8159 s, so absolute seconds are not comparable across sessions and only a before/after pair taken in one session is (`compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`).
- `ant compileAll` leaves the bytecode cache holding no library jars: the first `fortress compile` after a rebuild of the compiler clears `default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/`, and `fortress run` then dies with `NoClassDefFoundError: fortress/CompilerLibrary$GeneratorZZ32`; the library-order recompile of `repo-internals.md:170-179` restores it, about two minutes (observed 2026-09-17).
- The compiled path's bytecode cache can come up empty after a library-order rebuild that reports exit 0; re-running the same commands one at a time produced the jars (`perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md`).
- Generic instantiations are stamped out at class-load time by ASM rewriting of template bytecode (`InstantiatingClassloader.java`, `repo-internals.md:129`); whether `nat` parameters are baked into stamped classes is unprobed.
- Implicit parallelism: `for` is parallel unless every generator is `seq`; the elements of a tuple and the operands of an operator are evaluated in parallel implicit threads (`tuple-expr.tex:23-24`, `operator-app.tex:59`; row 265). `FORTRESS_THREADS` sizes the work-stealing pool; there is no explicit threading in any of our programs.
- The compile path's checker cannot check `nat` parameters at all (see the prelude section). Sizes in types (`nat` parameters) are "instantiated at runtime" by the specification (`trait-parameters.tex`, natparams); they check shapes when a value is made or passed; no optimization is built on them anywhere. A `nat`-typed parameter does not unify statically with a run-time-built array (row 23); the interpreter matches at dispatch, and a mismatch reads "Failed to find any matching overload", uncatchable (row 83). A literal size does unify (row 23's positive half).

## What the conformance review of the eight rungs established (2026-09-17, `reviews/rung-conformance-1-4.md` and `-5-8.md`, verified in this session)

- The review's first finding, a top-level mutable variable compiled outside the transaction, has been repaired: what the compiled path does now is the repair-batch entry in the ladder section below, the finding as it stood is in `FACTS-history.md` § What the conformance review of the eight rungs established, and the gate rule it exposed is the thread-count entry in that same section (`compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/REPORT.md`).
- **The team already folds `IntLiteral` arithmetic at compile time and warned against doing it at run time.** `IntegerLiteralFoldingVisitor.java` folds the operators in `BigInteger` and `phases/PhaseOrder.java:57,142` wires `INTEGERLITERALFOLDING` before `TYPECHECK`; three lines below the comparison block rung 6 cited by line number, `FortressBuiltin.fss` carries the team's comment, verbatim: "Do not enable these until coercion is implemented; doing so will cause all our arithmetic to occur on IntLiterals". Rung 7's run-time bodies are nonetheless genuinely needed, because folding is syntactic and cannot see a literal bound to a variable, which is the case its three files hit; what it landed without was the knowledge that the phase exists, so the throwing bodies read as unfinished work rather than as the bodies of a case the team meant to be folded away, and the two mechanisms now disagree on the same values: `println (4294967295 + 1)` folds to the correct `4294967296` while the same arithmetic through two variables gives `0`.
- **Citing `Specification/library/apis/*.tex` as an independent standard is circular.** `Specification/library/structure.tex:25-31` says in the team's own words that Part Library "is largely automatically generated from the API code for the libraries themselves" and that the libraries are "presently in a state of flux", so `library/apis/CompilerBuiltin.tex` is a rendering of `CompilerBuiltin.fsi` and cannot justify an edit to that same file. Two rung reports cited it as the published api or the spec's shape. The prose chapters of `Specification/basic/` and `basic-lib/` are the standard; the api renderings are not. Sharper still (2026-09-19, batch 1's record worker): the rendered `library/apis/*.tex` files are not in the tree at all, they are generated at spec-build time from the `.fsi` sources (`Specification/library/default-libraries.tex:27,39`), so the `(api listing)` citations of ledger rows 314 and 316 and of `library_tests/IntLiteralArithRung7.fss:30-31` name paths that cannot be opened; the `(api listing)` convention should cite the `.fsi` line instead.
- **The specification makes an integer literal arbitrary precision** (`basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-85`, a digits-only numeral having the value of the numeral interpreted in radix ten, with nothing bounding it), and gives wrapping its own operator spellings (`basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:369-370, 400-401`), so the literal wrap of ledger row 317 is a violation predating the ladder rather than an unaddressed case.

## Earlier performance work on record (missed by the coordinator on 2026-09-15 until Pavol pointed at it)

- `explorations/performance-roadmap.md` (2026-09-08, a proposal, not approved): the measured start (interpreter ~1000× CPython on microGPT; compiler 7-9× the interpreter; both paths run the same object protocol, every `RR64` a heap object, no native double arithmetic emitted; the checker off in `walk`); Phase 0 item 0.1 is exactly "turn the static checker on for `walk`" with the fact that `Shell.java` has no switch for it; 0.2 a benchmark harness (microGPT forward, backward, Adam step, plus the two scalar benches, on interpreter, compiler and CPython); Route A (unbox by static type A1, `double[]` arrays A2, static overload resolution A3, `invokedynamic` dispatch A4); Route B Truffle.
- `explorations/backend-options.md` (2026-08-23 conversation, recovered 09-08): Truffle on GraalVM ranked first among backends; the claims about tools unverified.
- A fact is searched in `INDEX.md`, which carries one line per standalone note under `explorations/`, before it is called absent; that rule is the correction the 2026-09-15 deficit produced, and the deficit itself is in `FACTS-history.md` § Earlier performance work on record.
- **Checked integer arithmetic keeps integer loops scalar on the JVM** (2026-09-17, from the rung 6 skeptic's overflow finding; recorded at length in `performance-roadmap.md` under "Corrections recorded on the way"): `+` on `ZZ32` binds to `jIntOverflowingAdd` (`LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:625`), whose helper (`nativeHelpers/simpleIntArith.java`) tests the sign bits and throws `IntegerOverflow`, which the spec mandates (`Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:114-117`; `⊞`/BOXPLUS is the wrapping operator, `CompilerBuiltin.fss:626`); HotSpot's SuperWord vectorizes only counted loops with no control flow in the body, so a branch per operation, however cheap scalar, forecloses SIMD. The consequence for the roadmap: step A5's "SIMD comes free from HotSpot" holds for floating-point loops, which is where microGPT's hot arithmetic is (`RR64`, no trapping), and not for the integer indices, counters and reductions around them, nor for A2's address arithmetic. Four remedies exist, cheapest first, and the roadmap lists them; none is worth doing before the loops are measured.

## What an autonomous climb costs in wall clock (measured 2026-09-17, `explorations/coordinator/iteration-cost.md`)

- **The eight-rung climb took 8h37m and every minute of it was serial**: 36 agents, no two ever overlapping, the sum of agent walls plus the 35 inter-agent gaps equalling the span exactly. Of the 508.3 agent-minutes, 57.8% was inside tool calls and 42.2% was model thinking, so no build optimization can buy back more than 57% of anything. The gate (`ant testFast` 14 runs at a 434 s median, `ant testSystem` 11 at 147.6 s) was 130.5 minutes, 25.2% of the clock; the ladder subset runs 64.9 and the library-order bytecode-cache rebuilds 44.6. `ant compileAll` ran exactly three times, in exactly the three rungs that touched `.java`/`.scala`, incremental at 46 s, and no cache rebuild ran over a still-valid cache: that discipline held. 41.0 minutes of gate produced no information, 21.7 of it because an agent piped `ant` through `tail` and had to re-run to see the summary it was required to grep, and 19.3 because a skeptic re-gated a byte-identical tree it had no mechanism to prove was fresh.
- **`ant testFast` cannot be made much faster by parallelism on this box**: its four tracks already occupy the four cores, one suite (`OtherCompilerJUTest`, 439.6 s) sets its wall, and the two gate targets run together have a realistic optimum of about 554 s against 583 s serial, 29 seconds, while sharing `test-caches`, `test-tmp` and `TEST-RESULTS` so they would need a `build.xml` change to be safe at all. Whole rungs in parallel worktrees buy nothing for the same reason: cores, not disk, are the constraint (a worktree costs 293 MB). What overlaps is a model-bound stage against a tool-bound one — `plan` is 68% model time and `implement` 76% tool.
- **The three-component bytecode-cache rebuild is 4.7× the five-component one** where the edit is downstream of `AnyType` and `CompilerBuiltin`: 24.6-30.4 s against 110-162 s, found by the rung 8 agents in the climb's last hour after 20 of 22 rebuilds had used the long form.

## The interpreter's library fed to the compiler (measured 2026-09-16, `perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md`)

- Only 211 of `FortressLibrary.fss`'s 4,518 lines (4.7%) are the 108 `builtinPrimitive` native bindings; the rest is plain Fortress. Whole interpreter library: 427 bindings across nine files. The interpreter's glue classes take the evaluator's boxed values and cannot be reused by the compiled path; the compiler's natives are static Java methods, and `nativeHelpers/` already ships 355 of them, covering about 79 of the 108 by another name.
- `fortress compile Library/FortressLibrary.fss` as it is: 1,417 errors, all in DISAMBIGUATE, all name collisions because both preludes are in scope; an artifact. With `FortressLibrary` made the prelude (a driver over `Shell`'s public entry points, no tracked file changed): disambiguation passes with zero errors; the type checker then reports 92 errors in the library's own apis (36 `X excludes Y but it extends Y`, 26 `types exclude each other`, 26 `Integral[\I\]` bound failures, in the comparison and numeric tower) and then **crashes: `Not yet implemented`** in `STypesUtil.makeInferenceArg` (STypesUtil.scala:546-559) for `nat`, `int`, `bool`, `dim` and `unit` static parameters. Desugar and codegen are never reached.
- **The Scala type checker does not implement `nat` static parameters at all**: a six-line program with a `nat` parameter fails on the compile path (`Not yet implemented` inferred, `ClassCastException` explicit) and runs on the interpreter. The interpreter's library has 81 such declarations, C4's vocabulary 30; `CompilerLibrary` has one, the empty `Matrix`. So the sized-array vocabulary cannot pass the compile path's checker today, and the static dimension checking the `nat` design promises is not implemented anywhere.
- Plain-Fortress library code without `nat`s passes the checker: `FlatArrays.fsi` type-checks with zero errors of its own against the interpreter prelude; its only failures are the prelude's and the `nat` crash. A minimal `Array`/`Vector` shim for the compiler's world is not possible; FlatArrays uses the array protocol (`fill`, `map`, `ivmap`, `t()`, `get`/`put`/`init0`/`replica`), which is `NativeArray.fss` plus about 1,000 lines of the library.
- Therefore "use FortressLibrary for the compiler too" is, in order: implement `nat`/`int`/`bool` static parameters in the checker; fix or relax the 92 tower errors; port the native bindings (the smallest part). Supersedes the coordinator's guess of 2026-09-15 that the library would "fail the checker in places nobody has counted": counted now, and the wall is the checker, not the library.

## A user grammar on the compile path (measured 2026-09-16, `perf-probes/grammar-compile/REPORT.md`)

- As shipped, a grammar-importing program stops at DISAMBIGUATE on the compile path with 1,342 errors, none in the program: every grammar api imports `FortressSyntax`, which imports `FortressAst`, which imports the interpreter's `FortressLibrary`, so the two preludes collide. The GRAMMAR phase is in the compiler's phase order and `GraphRepository.syntaxExpand` serves both worlds; what is missing is a compiler-world spelling of `FortressAst`/`FortressSyntax`.
- With two probe-only shims shadowing `FortressLibrary` and `List` on the source path, the collision is gone, Rats! runs under `fortress compile`, and a user grammar compiles to bytecode and runs (`twicep⦇ 21 ⦈` prints 42).
- Behind that wall the type checker does not know templates: there is no `TemplateGap`/`_SyntaxTransformation` case anywhere under `scala_src/typechecker/`. Consequences: an expansion in argument position must be parenthesized by the template text itself (`Argument to function must be parenthesized`); a template naming a function declared in the using component (ledger row 270, the mechanism the focused base's named functions rest on) crashes the post-typecheck assertion (`ClassCastException: BoxedUnit cannot be cast to AbstractNode`); a typed lambda written in a template (row 285) fails with `Unbound type: ZZ32`, the type never disambiguated. So rows 270, 282 and 285, the APL ladder's whole division of labour, are interpreter-only facts, and the APL microGPT cannot go through the compiler until the checker learns templates. Ledger rows 288-291 (merged 2026-09-16).

## The template-checking fix, prototyped under a classpath shadow (2026-09-16, `perf-probes/template-check/REPORT.md`)
- The plan's four edits (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala`, `STypesUtil.scala`, `ExprFactory.java`, `Transform.java`; 31 changed lines, `template-check/diffs/`) were compiled into `shadow-classes/` and put first on the classpath; no tracked file changed. Gate with the shadow overlaid on `ProjectFortress/build` and restored afterwards: `ant testFast` 1,377 tests 0 failures, `ant testSystem` 382 pass 0 fail 0 skip (`33-testfast.out`, `34-testsystem.out`).
- Row 285 (a typed lambda written whole in one template) is TRUE on the compile path behind the prelude shims: `u_lamp`, `u_app` and their `q` variants compile and print the interpreter's values (`22-`, `23-shadow-*.out`). m01-m07 all compile and print what the interpreter prints.
- Row 270 (a template naming a function declared in the using component) is true only when the grammar api is analysed in the same process (`24-shadow-dblp-uncached.out`); through the api cache it still fails on parenthesization, because `nodes_util/NodeReflection.getPrintableFields:218-244` writes only a `TemplateGap` node's declared fields, so its inherited `_info` (which carries the parenthesized flag) never reaches the `.tfi` file and reads back as a default. A fifth edit, letting a gap's inherited fields be written and read like any other node's, closes it (`extra-src/`, `25-extra-nodereflection.out`); it is measured only, not gated, and where the fix belongs is Pavol's call.

<!-- What Pavol has decided, stated, or already knows, with dates; in his words or a close paraphrase. Read at session start so that none of it is re-explained to him. Standing directives about how we work are in explorations/protocol.md and are not repeated here. -->

# Pavol's positions, decisions and known ground

## The goal

- The revival's toy problem is microGPT and the search is for its most readable expression; Fortress's mathematical notation and Iverson's APL notation (with Hsu's data design for data-flow algorithms) are the two sources; "we are searching for the optimal expression of the microGPT algorithm for readability" (2026-09-15).
- The APL side quest began as a curiosity (2026-09-10), became a ladder to learn APL (09-11, he has not read the book), was redirected to native code, not an interpreter in an interpreter (09-12), and got microGPT as its target on 09-13; the ladder "was to keep you busy and expand the probe". The remaining APL ground (tacit, characters, nested arrays) is not pursued (09-15).
- Hoped for a diamond from the Hsu-style flat program; got "a few lumps of coal"; the rewrite (rung 4b) was to get closer, and the vocabulary is where any polishing happens.

## History he knows (do not re-explain)

- DARPA's HPCS did not take Sun into phase three (2006) and the project lived on at Sun Labs until 2012. His reading: they did no work on performance, "mucked around with syntax", and the promise that a sufficiently advanced compiler would later make mathematical types fast was never true; the funding was pulled for good reason.
- The compiled path is only about ten times the interpreter because numerics are boxed (`FRR64`, no `DADD`); "without unboxed doubles and arrays of doubles, what are we even doing here"; this goes on the priority list (2026-09-15). The first measurement (the scalar loop) said boxing was about 2% of the gap; Pavol objected that the loop was an edge case microGPT never hits (literals in the loop, a `:=` accumulator) and asked for a fairer test; the fairer test agreed with him: on array-shaped code boxing is 6.3-6.5× and the dominant representational cost, and nothing microGPT-shaped compiles at all today (FACTS, execution model). The order now on record: the compiler library's array type first, the two one-line runtime defects second, unboxing designed into the first.
- The type checker runs only on the compile path; he wants it usable on interpreter programs and considers that low-hanging fruit (2026-09-15). It is item 0.1 of `performance-roadmap.md` (2026-09-08), which the coordinator had not indexed; see FACTS, deficit.
- Hsu's critique of language paradigms as accidental complexity; he is "coming around to his point of view".

## Decisions on record

- 2026-09-14: C4 is the APL target form; C2's tuple hyperparameter form is what a strand assignment expands to; the semicolon form is set aside.
- 2026-09-15: redo rung 4 as the focused base (done); do the vocabulary swap with shared `nat` dimensions (in progress); the ledger is not split, two views are derived (done); the ledger review is the next major step after the swap; the remaining APL ground is closed.
- 2026-09-15: "fleshing out the standard library" is a very important task: first fix the `RR64`/`AdditiveGroup` mismatch, then extend the algebraic layer (Ring, Field and what ML's matrices and tensors need) so the library's trait flavour reaches them. Open question he has not answered: whether this means editing the sealed `Library/` (the standing rule is never; worklist item 4 "unseal the linear-algebra layer" names the rows) or building the layer in our own tree; the coordinator assumes our own tree until he says otherwise.
- 2026-09-16: the goal restated: finish what the designers intended, judged by the latest committed spec (`Specification/`, the July 2012 draft), not redesign the language; the measuring stick is one program, microGPT compiled to bytecode and running fast; a pure-Java microGPT will be written later as the floor to measure against; the tree is tagged at the unsealing point and the next phase modifies the original sources with the lessons of the explorations.
- 2026-09-16: the mathematical notation (Fortify, the 2D rendering) is his verdict "a neat gimmick, not a good idea": it encodes one perspective on a computation into the syntax, and the same mathematics can be written many ways; APL's glyph-per-transformation is the purer realisation. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn a PhaseProbe capture into the classified hole list of the report.

usage: classify.py <capture.out> [<capture-with-DECL-CRASH.out>]

The second argument, if given, supplies the set of top-level declarations the
type checker crashed on, so that code-generation failures on a declaration that
never got annotations can be told apart from the rest.  It defaults to the
first.
"""
import sys, io, re, collections, os

cap = sys.argv[1]
crashsrc = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else cap
ROOT = "/home/user/fortress/"

def rows(path):
    out = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for raw in io.open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
        if raw.startswith("@@"):
            f = raw.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
            out[f[0]].append(f[1:])
    return out

R = rows(cap)
CR = rows(crashsrc)
unchecked = set(f[1] for f in CR.get("@@TC DECL-CRASH", []))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the classes
def klass(site, msg):
    m = msg or ""
    if "Null.unwrap" in site or "None$.get" in site:            return "T no type annotation"
    if "Missing type information" in m:                          return "T no type annotation"
    if "lacks type information" in m:                            return "T no type annotation"
    if "Return type is not inferred" in m:                       return "T no type annotation"
    if "Can't compile Juxt" in m:                                return "V no visitor: Juxt"
    if "Can't compile Label" in m or "Can't compile Exit" in m:  return "V no visitor: Label/Exit"
    if "Can't compile AmbiguousMultifixOpExpr" in m:             return "V no visitor: AmbiguousMultifixOpExpr"
    if "Can't compile" in m and "sayWhat" in site:               return "V no visitor: other"
    if "Don't know how to compile this kind of FnDecl" in m:     return "C canCompile refuses"
    if "forIntArg" in site:                                      return "N nat static argument"
    if "OverloadSet.split" in site:                              return "O malformed overload set"
    if "kind env" in m:                                          return "K kind env / trait table"
    if "Not in the trait table" in m:                            return "K kind env / trait table"
    if "RTTI" in m or "static args of generic types" in m:       return "R type reference / RTTI"
    if "VarArgs" in m:                                           return "R type reference / RTTI"
    if "Forbid clauses" in m:                                    return "X other: forbid clause"
    if "forMethodInvocation" in site:                            return "X other: intersection receiver"
    return "X other"

def report(tag, label):
    if tag not in R: return
    per_class = collections.Counter()

#!/bin/bash
# Every command this probe ran, in order.  Run from anywhere:
#
#   ./explorations/perf-probes/prelude/desugar-codegen/run-all.sh <work-dir>
#
# <work-dir> is a scratch directory OUTSIDE the repository: the compiled driver,
# the shadow sources and classes, and a private Fortress cache all live there.
# Nothing is written to default_repository/ and no tracked file is modified.
#
# The captures beside this script are the raw output with the stack-trace lines
# removed (`trim` below); the raw output stays in the work directory.
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../.."                     # $FORTRESS_HOME
source experiment/env.sh                             # JDK 25, FORTRESS_THREADS=1, -Xmx4g -Xss64m
P=explorations/perf-probes/prelude/desugar-codegen
W=${1:?usage: run-all.sh <work-dir>}
mkdir -p "$W"
CP=$(./bin/fortress_classpath 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | sed 's#:.*/default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache##')

# 0. the driver and the shadow classes
javac -nowarn -cp "$CP" -d "$W/classes" $P/PhaseProbe.java
$P/make-shadows.sh "$W/shadow-src" "$W/shadow-classes"

run () {   # run <out> <probe args...>;  PROBE_JFLAGS carries the -Dprobe.* switches
  local out=$1; shift
  rm -rf "$W/caches"; mkdir -p "$W/caches"
  { echo "########## PhaseProbe $*"; date -u +'# start %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'; S=$(date +%s)
    java $JAVA_FLAGS -XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow -Dfortress.caches="$W/caches" ${PROBE_JFLAGS:-} \
         -cp "$W/shadow-classes:$W/classes:$CP" PhaseProbe "$@"
    echo "exit=$?"; echo "ELAPSED $(( $(date +%s) - S )) s"; } > "$W/$out" 2>&1
  echo "ran $out"
}
trim () {  # keep the diagnostics, drop the stack-trace lines
  grep -v '^@@CG AT\|^@@CG PREAT\|^@@CG OVLAT\|^@@CG CAT\|^@@TC DECLAT' "$W/$1" > "$P/$1"
}
dedup () { # distinct lines only, each cut to 240 columns (the checker's messages are long)
  awk '!seen[$0]++' "$W/$1" | cut -c1-240 > "$P/$1"
}

# 1. reference: the compile path as it is, on the interpreter's library.
#    Dies in the checker at STypesUtil.makeInferenceArg (the `nat` gap).
run 01-reference-full.out -order full Library/FortressLibrary.fss

# 2. method (1): the same phases with TYPECHECK left out of the order.
#    DESUGAR refuses to run at all without the checker's STypeChecker map
#    (AnalyzeResult.java:93) -- this capture is taken with the shadow DesugarPhase
#    disabled, by putting the shadow classes last instead of first.
  rm -rf "$W/caches"; mkdir -p "$W/caches"
  { echo "########## PhaseProbe -order nocheck-desugar (shadow classes NOT on the path)"
    java $JAVA_FLAGS -Dfortress.caches="$W/caches" -cp "$W/classes:$CP" \

    echo "exit=$?"; } > "$P/02-nocheck-desugar-refused.out" 2>&1

cp "$W/03-nocheck-through-overloadrewrite.out" "$P/"

# 4. the control that decides method (1): the COMPILER's own library, which
#    compiles green, with and without TYPECHECK, and under the tolerant checker
run 04-control-compilerlib-full.out    -order full            -compilerlib Library/CompilerLibrary.fss
trim 04-control-compilerlib-full.out
run 05-control-compilerlib-nocheck.out -order nocheck-codegen -compilerlib Library/CompilerLibrary.fss
cp "$W/05-control-compilerlib-nocheck.out" "$P/"
PROBE_JFLAGS=-Dprobe.tolerant=true \
run 06-control-compilerlib-tolerant.out -order full -compilerlib Library/CompilerLibrary.fss
trim 06-control-compilerlib-tolerant.out

run 07-nocheck-codegen.out -order nocheck-codegen Library/FortressLibrary.fss

input.content:
<!-- What the compile path's DESUGAR and CODEGEN phases do with the interpreter's own library, measured 2026-09-20 by a delegated worker. The checker crashes on `nat` before desugaring, so it is stepped around, not fixed; §2 says which of the two ways worked and what its caveat is. Every number comes from a capture named in the Artifacts table; the driver, the shadow generator and the classifier are beside them under `desugar-codegen/`. Nothing tracked was modified; the runs used a private cache outside the repository and `ant` was not run. -->

# Desugaring and code generation on the interpreter's library

Nobody had ever run the compile path's later phases on `Library/FortressLibrary.fss`
and `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss`: the type checker stops
them first, with 93 errors and then a hard crash on the `nat`-kinded static
parameters the library is built out of (`coordinator/two-libraries.md` §3,
`perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md` §2). This is the hole list from the other side of
that wall, classified, and nothing else. It recommends nothing.

**The short answer.** DESUGAR and OVERLOADREWRITE accept the whole 4,507-line
library with zero diagnostics. Code generation then refuses 313 declarations and
emits 275. Of the 313, **5 are on a declaration the checker had checked without
complaint**: four are the same `nat` gap, now on the code generator's side rather
than the checker's, and one is a method call on an intersection-typed receiver.
The other 308 are downstream of the checker — 112 on declarations it crashed on,
96 on declarations it reported errors on, 100 on the overload dispatch
declarations a later phase synthesizes. The code generator refuses nothing by
`canCompile` in this library, and `builtinPrimitive` produces no code-generation
failure at all.

---

## 1. Setup

Tree at `92d97379c`; the commits since `6af77573a` are documents only, no file
under `Library/` or `ProjectFortress/` changed. JDK 25.0.3,
`source experiment/env.sh` (`FORTRESS_THREADS=1`, `-Xmx4g -Xss64m`),
`-XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow` so that a `ClassCastException` carries its
frames, and `-Dfortress.caches` pointing at a scratch directory outside the
repository, wiped before every run (`ProjectProperties.java:283`).
`default_repository/` was not touched, `ant` was not run, and no tracked file was
modified. Every command is in `desugar-codegen/run-all.sh`.

The driver, `desugar-codegen/PhaseProbe.java`, is built only from public `Shell`
entry points, exactly as the earlier probe's `WorldFlip.java` is: it sets the
interpreter's prelude (`Shell.useInterpreterLibraries()`), then puts the compile
path's own desugaring settings back on top of it —
`setExtendsObjectPreDesugaring(true)` and `setCompiledExprDesugaring(true)`,
which `useInterpreterLibraries()` turns off (`Shell.java:371-386`) — and then
chooses a phase order. Running with the interpreter's desugaring settings instead
is a flag (`-interpdesugar`), and so is running the compiler's own prelude
(`-compilerlib`), which is the control.

## 2. The two methods, and which one produced the list

### 2.1 Method (1): leave TYPECHECK out of the phase order

`PhaseOrder` is a public enum and `Shell.setPhaseOrder` takes any array of it, so
the compiler's order minus TYPECHECK is one line in the driver.

Through PRETYPECHECKDESUGAR and INTEGERLITERALFOLDING the library passes with
`rc=0` and no diagnostics. **DESUGAR then refuses to run at all, and not for want
of type annotations**: `DesugarPhase.execute` reads `previous.typeCheckers()`
(`phases/DesugarPhase.java:43`), and `AnalyzeResult.typeCheckers()` throws
*"A compiler pass is trying to get access to the type chekcers when it should
not"* when that map is null, which it is unless `TypeCheckPhase` built it
(`AnalyzeResult.java:93`; capture `02-nocheck-desugar-refused.out`). The map is
passed on for exactly one thing, `CaseExprDesugarer` (`Desugarer.java:120-123`).
With a shadow `DesugarPhase` that hands it an empty map, **DESUGAR and
OVERLOADREWRITE both pass the whole library with zero errors**, `rc=0` in 15 s
(`03-nocheck-through-overloadrewrite.out`).

CODEGEN then fails.

### 2.2 The control that settles method (1)

`Library/CompilerLibrary.fss` — the compiler's *own* prelude, which compiles
green — was put through the same two orders.

| run | order | result |
|---|---|---|
| `04-control-compilerlib-full.out` | compiler's order, unchanged | 162 declarations emitted, component OK, `rc=0`, 40 s |
| `05-control-compilerlib-nocheck.out` | same, TYPECHECK removed | dies at `CompilerLibrary.fss:176:33`, `Can't compile Juxt`, `CodeGen.defaultCase:1670`, 4 s |

A juxtaposition is what the type checker resolves into a function application or
a method invocation; `CodeGen` has no `forJuxt`. So without the checker every
juxtaposition in any program is a code-generation hole, and a hole list taken
that way is a list of the checker's absence. Measured on the interpreter's
library with the code generator made tolerant per declaration
(`07-nocheck-codegen.out`): **482 failures**, of which 335 are missing type
annotations and 124 are `Juxt`; **161 of them are on declarations that the
checker, when it is allowed to run, checks without complaint.**

Method (1) therefore produced no usable list. It is reported because it settles
the question the brief put first, and because the DESUGAR result above — the
whole library through desugaring and overload rewriting with zero diagnostics —
is only visible this way.

### 2.3 Method (2): TYPECHECK in the order, its failures caught per declaration

This produced the list. Three shadow classes, generated from the tracked sources
by a textual patch (`desugar-codegen/shadow-patch.py`) and put first on the
classpath; the tracked files are untouched. All the probe behaviour is behind
`-Dprobe.tolerant=true`, so the same classes behave like the originals without
it.

* `StaticChecker` checks the component **one top-level declaration at a time**.
  This is the same traversal split up: the `SComponent` case of
  `impls/Decls.scala:77-81` maps `check` over the declarations with no added
  environment, and `STypeChecker.typeCheck` takes any `Node`
  (`STypeChecker.scala:430`). A declaration whose check throws is reported and
  **kept unchecked** rather than dropped — an earlier variant that dropped them
  punched a hole in the trait table and moved the failure to
  `Not in the trait table: FortressLibrary.Number`.
* `TypeCheckPhase` reports the error count instead of raising
  `MultipleStaticError`, so the partly annotated component travels on to DESUGAR,
  OVERLOADREWRITE and CODEGEN.
* `CodeGen` and `CodeGenerationPhase` catch per declaration in each of the four
  places code generation can fail before the next declaration is reached:
  `CodeGen`'s constructor (which computes inherited methods for every trait in
  the component, `CodeGen.java:481`), overload dispatch generation
  (`generateTopLevelOverloads`), the object/variable pre-pass
  (`forComponent`'s second loop), and the top-level declaration loop. After a
  catch the probe puts back the state that `forTraitDecl`/`forObjectDecl` set on
  the way in and clear on the way out — `inATrait`, `inAnObject`,
  `currentTraitObjectDecl`, `traitOrObjectName`, `mv` — because there is no
  `try`/`finally` around them (`CodeGen.java:4034-4037`, `:4276-4417`,

# Desugaring and code generation on the interpreter's library

Nobody had ever run the compile path's later phases on `Library/FortressLibrary.fss`
and `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss`: the type checker stops
them first, with 93 errors and then a hard crash on the `nat`-kinded static
parameters the library is built out of (`coordinator/two-libraries.md` §3,
`perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md` §2). This is the hole list from the other side of
that wall, classified, and nothing else. It recommends nothing.

**The short answer.** DESUGAR and OVERLOADREWRITE accept the whole 4,507-line
library with zero diagnostics. Code generation then refuses 313 declarations and
emits 275. Of the 313, **5 are on a declaration the checker had checked without
complaint**: four are the same `nat` gap, now on the code generator's side rather
than the checker's, and one is a method call on an intersection-typed receiver.
The other 308 are downstream of the checker — 112 on declarations it crashed on,
96 on declarations it reported errors on, 100 on the overload dispatch
declarations a later phase synthesizes. The code generator refuses nothing by
`canCompile` in this library, and `builtinPrimitive` produces no code-generation
failure at all.

## 1. Setup

Tree at `92d97379c`; the commits since `6af77573a` are documents only, no file
under `Library/` or `ProjectFortress/` changed. JDK 25.0.3,
`source experiment/env.sh` (`FORTRESS_THREADS=1`, `-Xmx4g -Xss64m`),
`-XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow` so that a `ClassCastException` carries its
frames, and `-Dfortress.caches` pointing at a scratch directory outside the
repository, wiped before every run (`ProjectProperties.java:283`).
`default_repository/` was not touched, `ant` was not run, and no tracked file was
modified. Every command is in `desugar-codegen/run-all.sh`.

The driver, `desugar-codegen/PhaseProbe.java`, is built only from public `Shell`
entry points, exactly as the earlier probe's `WorldFlip.java` is: it sets the
interpreter's prelude (`Shell.useInterpreterLibraries()`), then puts the compile
path's own desugaring settings back on top of it —
`setExtendsObjectPreDesugaring(true)` and `setCompiledExprDesugaring(true)`,
which `useInterpreterLibraries()` turns off (`Shell.java:371-386`) — and then
chooses a phase order. Running with the interpreter's desugaring settings instead
is a flag (`-interpdesugar`), and so is running the compiler's own prelude
(`-compilerlib`), which is the control.

component OK, `rc=0`, 40 s (`06-control-compilerlib-tolerant.out` against
`04-control-compilerlib-full.out`). The machinery does not change a compile that
works.

## 3. Caveats

1. **112 of 446 declarations reach code generation with no annotations**, because
   the checker crashed on them. Their failures are not evidence about code
   generation, and the tables below separate them.
2. **96 more reach it annotated by a checker that reported errors on them.** The
   checker signals an error and leaves the subtree it could not finish untyped;
   those failures would go away if the library type-checked cleanly, and are also
   separated below.
3. **Overload dispatch generation had to be switched off** (`-Dprobe.skipOverloads`).
   With it on, `CodeGen.generateTopLevelOverloads` → `OverloadSet.split` →
   `OverloadingOracle.lteq` → `TypeAnalyzer.pExc`/`excludesClause` ran **1,046 s
   without emitting a single declaration** and was stopped by hand
   (`12-overloads-not-skipped.out`; the same phase takes 40 s over the whole of
   the compiler's library). Seven overload sets had failed by then, all with the
   same message, and they are in the table below. With the switch on,
   `topLevelOverloadedNamesAndSigs` is empty, which changes naming decisions at
   `CodeGen.java:3332` and `:3513`; the 100 failures on synthesized
   `_RewriteFnOverloadDecl`s below are therefore a floor, not a measurement of
   what overload dispatch generation would do.
4. **The compile path's desugaring settings are on** (§1), which is what "through
   the compile path's phases" means, and they are not free: see §4.3.
5. The list is a first pass. `CodeGen` writes into one class writer as it goes,
   and although the probe restores the declaration-level state (§2.3) it cannot
   undo a half-written method. The classes and their proportions are the finding;
   an individual row after the first failure in its class is not certified.
6. The banner line of `08-tolerant-codegen.out` and `12-overloads-not-skipped.out`
   predates a cosmetic rename in the driver's print; the phases and settings it
   prints are the same as the others'.

## 4. What each phase did

### 4.1 Before the checker

DISAMBIGUATE: zero errors, as already on record. PRETYPECHECKDESUGAR and
INTEGERLITERALFOLDING: zero errors. This includes the compile path's own
pre-desugarings — the `extends Object` rewrite of unbounded static parameters and
the compound/tuple-assignment and subscript rewrite
(`AssignmentAndSubscriptDesugarer`, compile path only, `Shell.java:268-270`).

### 4.2 DESUGAR and OVERLOADREWRITE

**Zero diagnostics on the whole library, in both methods.** Coercion desugaring,
getter/setter desugaring, typecase desugaring, type-ascription desugaring and the
bodyless-`FnDecl`-to-abstract marking all run (the last three only because the
driver turns `compiled_expr_desugaring` on), and none of them complains. The
answer to "what does the compile path's desugaring make of the interpreter's
library" is: nothing to report. `Desugarer.desugarApi` is a no-op by construction
(`Desugarer.java:82-85`); the component goes through untroubled.

### 4.3 What the compile path's desugaring costs the *checker*

This is where the interpreter/compiler desugaring difference shows, and it shows
one phase earlier than the brief expected. The same library, same checker, the
two desugaring settings (`10-typecheck-compilerdesugar.census.txt`,
`11-typecheck-interpdesugar.census.txt`):

| | compile path's desugaring | interpreter's |
|---|---|---|
| errors raised in the twelve prelude apis | **960** | **250** |
| of those, distinct | 257 | **93** |
| of those, `does not satisfy the corresponding bound Object` | **712** | **0** |
| errors raised in the 4,507-line component | **1,204** | **658** |
| of those, `… bound Object` | **618** | **0** |
| declarations the checker crashed on | 112 | 113 |

The 250 reproduce the record exactly: `FortressLibrary` 110, `RangeInternals`
104, `FortressBuiltin` 18, `String` 12, `List` 2, `FlatString` 4, the rest 0, and
they deduplicate to **93 distinct lines** — the number `two-libraries.md` §3
reports. The extra 712 come
from one switch: `setExtendsObjectPreDesugaring(true)` makes
`PreDisambiguationDesugaringVisitor.forStaticParam` (`:134-148`) give every
unbounded static parameter an `extends Object` bound, and the checker then
rejects every instantiation of such a parameter at a **tuple type** —
`Ill-formed type: Condition[\()\]`, `Comprehension[\(T,U)\]`, `Just[\(I,J)\]`,
`Generator[\(T,U)\]`, `ZeroIndexed[\(E,F)\]`, `Range[\(I,J,K)\]` and so on. A
tuple type is not a subtype of `Object` in this checker, and the interpreter's
library instantiates generics at tuple types everywhere.

This is the third item on the brief's list of desugarings the compile path
applies and the interpreter does not, and it is the largest single thing standing
between one library text and the compile path — larger than the 93 tower errors
already on record. It costs no code-generation failure, because it never gets
that far.

### 4.4 CODEGEN

Reached, and completed, for both files.

## 5. The counts

### 5.1 `Library/FortressLibrary.fss`, method (2) — `08-tolerant-codegen.out`

4,507 lines, **446 top-level declarations** (243 `FnDecl`, 103 `ObjectDecl`,
98 `TraitDecl`, 2 `VarDecl`). 703 s.

|---|---|
| checked, no error of its own | 237 |

**CODEGEN**, in the four places it can fail:

| stage | emitted | refused |
|---|---|---|
| `CodeGen`'s constructor, inherited methods per trait (`CodeGen.java:481`) | — | **1** |
| overload dispatch generation | — | switched off, caveat 3 |
| the object/variable pre-pass (`forComponent`, second loop) | — | **41** |
| the top-level declaration loop | **275** | **271** |
| **total** | **275** | **313** |

## 6. The distance

Of the 446 top-level declarations of the interpreter's library, the compile
path's checker gets through 334 and crashes on 112; desugaring and overload
rewriting then accept every one of them without a word; and of the 546
declarations that reach the code generator, 275 are emitted and 271 refused —
but only **5 refusals are on a declaration that type-checked cleanly**, four of
them the same `nat`-as-static-argument gap the checker has and one a method call
on an intersection-typed receiver, so the distance from here to code generation
for this library is not a list of missing visitors or refused constructs (there
are none of the latter and the `Juxt` failures are the checker's shadow, not the
code generator's) but the checker itself, plus the 712 tuple-at-`Object` errors
that the compile path's own `extends Object` pre-desugaring adds before it, plus
an overload dispatch generator that does not terminate on this library's
exclusion graph.

---

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `desugar-codegen/run-all.sh` | every command, in order; takes a scratch work directory |
| `desugar-codegen/PhaseProbe.java` | the driver: prelude, desugaring settings, phase order, all through public `Shell` entry points |
| `desugar-codegen/shadow-patch.py`, `make-shadows.sh` | generate and compile the four shadow classes from the tracked sources by textual patch |
| `desugar-codegen/classify.py` | turns a capture into the tables of §5 and the row-per-failure appendix |
| `01-reference-full.out` | the compile path as it is on `FortressLibrary`: `Not yet implemented`, 16 s |
| `02-nocheck-desugar-refused.out` | DESUGAR without TYPECHECK, no shadow: `AnalyzeResult.typeCheckers()` throws |
| `03-nocheck-through-overloadrewrite.out` | with the shadow: DESUGAR + OVERLOADREWRITE, `rc=0`, zero errors |
| `04-`, `05-`, `06-control-compilerlib-*.out` | the compiler's own library: green, green-minus-TYPECHECK, green-under-the-tolerant-checker |
| `07-nocheck-codegen.out`, `.classified.txt` | method (1)'s list: 482 failures, 161 of them on declarations the checker checks clean |
| `08-tolerant-codegen.out`, `.classified.txt` | **method (2)'s list**: the 313 failures, one row each, with class, provenance, span, exception, site and source line |
| `09-tolerant-builtin.out`, `.classified.txt` | the same for `FortressBuiltin.fss` |
| `10-`, `11-typecheck-*.census.txt` | the checker's errors under the two desugaring settings, every distinct message with its multiplicity |
| `12-overloads-not-skipped.out` | overload dispatch generation left on: 7 failures, then 1,046 s with no declaration emitted, stopped by hand |

Desugaring and code generation on the interpreter's library, measured

Nobody had run the compile path's DESUGAR and CODEGEN phases on
Library/FortressLibrary.fss: the type checker crashes on its nat-kinded
static parameters first. Two ways round the crash were tried.

Leaving TYPECHECK out of the phase order does not work, and the control
says why: the compiler's own CompilerLibrary.fss, which compiles green in
40 s, dies at the first juxtaposition without the checker, because CodeGen
has no forJuxt. A hole list taken that way is a list of the checker's
absence -- 482 failures on the interpreter's library, 161 of them on
declarations the checker checks without complaint.

What worked is keeping TYPECHECK in and catching its failures per top-level
declaration, so the rest travel on annotated. Validated against the
compiler's own library, where the tolerant run is identical to the ordinary
one. Of FortressLibrary's 446 top-level declarations the checker gets
through 334 and crashes on 112; DESUGAR and OVERLOADREWRITE then accept
every one of them with zero diagnostics; code generation emits 275 and
refuses 313. Five of the 313 are on a declaration that type-checked
cleanly: four are a static argument that is a number rather than a type
(nat s0, Rank[\1\]), the same gap as the checker's, and one is a method
call on an intersection-typed receiver. No construct is refused by
canCompile, and builtinPrimitive appears in no code-generation diagnostic.

Two further measurements. The compile path's own extends-Object
pre-desugaring, which useInterpreterLibraries turns off, adds 712 of the
960 checker errors in the prelude apis and 618 of the 1,204 in the
component: it rejects every generic instantiated at a tuple type. And
overload dispatch generation does not terminate usefully on this library's
exclusion graph -- 1,046 s without a declaration emitted, stopped by hand
-- so it had to be switched off to reach the declarations at all.

The report classifies all 313 by phase, class and provenance; the driver,
the shadow generator, the classifier and every capture are beside it.

Delivered: `explorations/perf-probes/prelude/desugar-codegen.md` + driver, shadows, classifier and 15 captures under `desugar-codegen/`. Committed `e5d8cdbd2`, pushed to `origin main` and `origin main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8`. Private cache outside the repo, FORTRESS_THREADS=1, no ant, no tracked file changed.

**Method that worked — (2), not (1).** Omitting TYPECHECK fails by construction: DESUGAR reads `previous.typeCheckers()` (`DesugarPhase.java:43`) and throws when TYPECHECK did not run. With a shadow that hands it an empty map, DESUGAR + OVERLOADREWRITE accept the whole 4,507-line library with **zero diagnostics**, but CODEGEN is then meaningless — the control settles it: the compiler's own `CompilerLibrary.fss`, green in 40 s, dies at the first juxtaposition without the checker (`Can't compile Juxt`, no `forJuxt`); method (1) on the interpreter's library gives 482 failures, 161 on declarations the checker checks clean. Method (2) keeps TYPECHECK and catches its failures per top-level declaration (keeping the declaration unchecked, not dropping it); validated on `CompilerLibrary.fss`, where it is identical to the ordinary compile (162 checked, 162 emitted, rc=0). Caveats: overload dispatch generation had to be switched off (1,046 s, no declaration emitted, stopped by hand); 112 declarations reach codegen unannotated; the compile path's desugaring settings are on.

**Counts, `FortressLibrary.fss` (446 top-level declarations).** TYPECHECK: 237 clean, 97 with errors, **112 crashed** (81 `nyi` at `makeInferenceArg`, 29 `TraitType→IntExpr` at `forIntArg`, 2 other). DESUGAR, OVERLOADREWRITE: 0 errors. CODEGEN: **275 emitted, 313 refused** — 1 in CodeGen's constructor, 41 in the object/variable pre-pass, 271 in the declaration loop. By class: T annotation missing 227, V no visitor 55 (53 `Juxt`, 1 `Label`, 1 `AmbiguousMultifixOpExpr`), N `nat` static argument 14, O malformed overload set 7, R type-reference/RTTI 6, K kind env/trait table 2, X other 2, **`canCompile` refusals 0, native bindings 0**. By provenance: 112 on declarations the checker crashed on, 96 on ones it reported errors on, 100 on synthesized `_RewriteFnOverloadDecl`s, **5 on declarations it checked clean**. `FortressBuiltin.fss`: 13/5 at TYPECHECK, 16 emitted / 26 refused, none on a cleanly checked declaration.

**Side measurement worth flagging:** the compile path's own `extends Object` pre-desugaring (`Shell.java:371-386`) adds **712 of the 960** checker errors in the prelude apis and **618 of 1,204** in the component — it rejects every generic instantiated at a tuple type. Bigger than the 93 tower errors on record, and it never reaches DESUGAR.

**Distance, one sentence:** desugaring is not a problem at all and code generation is nearly not one — only 5 of 446 declarations that type-check cleanly are refused (four a static argument that is a number rather than a type, one a method call on an intersection-typed receiver) — so what stands between the interpreter's library and bytecode is the checker itself, the 712 tuple-at-`Object` errors the compile path's own pre-desugaring adds ahead of it, and an overload dispatch generator that does not terminate on this library's exclusion graph.
